title: Ephemeral fallback: partial-response folding and graceful streaming under overload
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement: During large multi-region traffic spikes we want to avoid hard failures for streaming generation calls while preserving latency SLOs. Existing shedding policies either reject low-priority requests or fall back to a smaller model variant which can cause abrupt quality cliffs or long tail latencies for streaming clients. Goal: implement an ephemeral fallback mode that allows the runtime to 'fold' responses into a graceful partial stream with explicit degradation metadata, enabling clients to present partial/placeholder content or automatically request continuation when capacity stabilizes.

Core ideas: 
- Partial-response folding: when admission controller decides to degrade a streaming request, runtime emits a stable prefix followed by a short placeholder token stream and a final 'degraded' marker rather than failing outright. This preserves streaming UX and bounded latency.
- Ephemeral fallback variant: a lightweight runtime path that produces compressed/templated outputs (short summaries, extracted key points, or placeholder tokens) with a consistent latency bound (e.g., <150ms first byte).
- Degradation metadata: responses include structured headers/stream frames like X-Redwood-Degradation: true, Degradation-Mode: folding, Fold-Reason: capacity-shed, and a short continuation_token that clients can use to request resumed full fidelity when available.
- Backoff & continuation: the console/operator can configure a per-tenant continuation window. Clients requesting continuation present the continuation_token and are enqueued with elevated priority but still limited by the same admission controller.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) New runtime path implemented behind feature flag 'partial_folding_v1' that activates when (a) streaming=true and (b) admission controller chooses degrade and (c) request matches allowed degradation policy (per-customer opt-in).
2) API-level contract: streaming protocol adds final JSON control frame {"folded":true, "mode":"summary", "continuation_token":"xxx"}. SDKs can detect folded streams and surface UI affordances.
3) SLO impact: under a simulated 3x overload traffic profile, p99 tail latency for non-degraded streams must remain within current SLO; degraded streams should have bounded first-byte latency and documented quality reduction.
4) Telemetry: expose metrics: runtime.folding.count, runtime.folding.latency_p50/p90/p99, runtime.folding.continuations.accepted/rejected, and tag by tenant+region+model. Dashboards added in Grafana folder 'Reliability/Folding'.

Design notes & constraints: 
- We must avoid introducing request amplification: continuation attempts should be rate-limited and count against tenant budgets.
- Security: continuation_token is short-lived (TTL 5m) and opaque; it should be logged only at trace level, not stored in long-term logs.
- Client SDK changes are minimally invasive: SDKs receive one additional control frame and surface a boolean and continuation token. Web/Console will show a fallback banner when folded.
- Rollout plan: start in staging behind feature flag; canary to 5% of hostnames; monitor p95/p99 latency and error rates for both folded and non-folded flows.

Implementation plan (high level): 
1) Runtime: implement folding emitter in the streaming pipeline (C++/Rust path) with configuration knobs for fold length and placeholder types.
2) Admission: add 'degrade-with-fold' action to admission controller decisions.
3) API/SDK: define control frame spec and update Node/Python SDKs to decode it.
4) Telemetry & dashboard: instrument counters and add dashboard panels.
5) Canaries & runbook: add operator runbook for when folding rates spike unexpectedly (links below).

Links & artifacts: 
- Design spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/EPHEMERAL-FOLDING-DESIGN
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127 (initial emitter)
- SDK patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/129 (decode control frame)
- Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rel/folding
- Load test harness: https://buildkite.com/redwood-lfs/folding-loadtest (job 771)

Operator runbook excerpt: 
- If folding rate > 20% and customer impact is high, trigger Triage and consider scaling Dedicated pool or temporarily relaxing batching.
- To disable folding globally: flip feature flag partial_folding_v1 to off and enable fallback to reject or small-variant model.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: aligned with PM and Design to allow opt-in per customer. Action: Ravi to scope runtime changes; Avery to draft API control frame spec.
2025-02-18 - Prototype emitter complete in runtime branch. Initial measurements show first-byte <120ms for folded streams. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127

2025-02-21 - Engineering review: Miguel suggested moving continuation_token encoding to HMAC-signed blob to avoid extra DB lookups. Decision: use HMAC with short TTL; store minimal metadata in ephemeral cache only when required.
2025-02-25 - SDK update landed (node). UI design for 'folded' banner approved by Maya. SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/129

2025-02-27 - Load tests: under 3x synthetic spike, folded flows preserved host p99 latency but increased continuation queue length. Trade-off: improved UX vs additional continuation pressure. Next: add circuit-breaker on continuation acceptance per tenant.
2025-03-03 - Added per-tenant continuation backpressure and metric tags. Preparing canary to 5% in us-west-2 tomorrow.
